item.title: Optimum Prepares to File for Bankruptcy — What It Means for Customers
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: The national ISP Optimum will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy this fall, but what does that mean for customers?
item.content:encoded:
Optimum’s creditors want their money back

As reported earlier this week, New York-based internet service provider Optimum is expected to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy by the end of 2026. In a nutshell, creditors are forcing a reorganization of Optimum because of roughly $26 billion of debt. But what does that mean for existing Optimum customers and folks currently looking for service in Optimum areas? Read on to find out.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Has rapid expansion benefited Optimum customers?

Leveraging debt, Optimum bought up Suddenlink and Cablevision roughly 10 years ago to increase its footprint and profits. The potential profits have taken a back seat to debt repayment, and the cable giant has recently streamlined its cable TV service and increased its internet speeds to remain competitive in a market led by fiber and 5G providers. The same goes for starting prices. Optimum home internet pricing remained relatively flat from 2020–2025, as CableTV.com previously reported, standing out in an inflation-addled economy. Optimum service can sound competitive on paper, but our annual customer satisfaction survey results tell a very different story. Optimum customers came in last place in our 2026 cable TV survey, and Optimum internet service placed in the lowest quartile of overall customer satisfaction, too. So, although advertised internet speeds rose and internet pricing beat inflation, it appears that the debt from footprint expansion has done little to improve customer experience and worried its creditors in the process.

Will Optimum service continue to operate as usual?

Optimum is not going out of business, but the ownership structure is expected to change, which could lead to radical restructuring. Although we don’t know all of the details of the restructuring, recent history demonstrates that it’s likely Optimum will continue to deliver service at similar levels. For example, DISH filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy this summer, and DISH satellite customers have enjoyed uninterrupted service though the summer and into the fall. That said, DISH raised prices by $5 per month shortly thereafter in September 2026. Considering Optimum’s current debt load and below-market internet pricing, we think it’s likely Optimum will raise its prices again after filing for bankruptcy to help pay down more debt. We’ll keep monitoring the situation, so stay tuned!

In this article

Optimum

Although we don’t see Optimum service changing drastically after its bankruptcy filing, and its first-year internet pricing is very competitive, we say go with another provider because of Optimum’s low customer satisfaction and meh TV plans.

DISH Network

Bankruptcy is just one indicator that DISH has been on the decline for the past three or four years. We say go with DIRECTV if you’re looking for traditional satellite service or if you want the look and feel of cable in a streaming service.

item.title: Tired of TV Ad Tracking? Why People Are Using AI To Dumb Down Smart TVs
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Sick of ads on your TV operating system? Here’s why people are using AI vibescoding to make their smart TVs dumb.
item.content:encoded:
It’s virtually impossible to find a non-smart TV in stores these days, but they also come with frustrations like bloat, banner ads, content trackers, and slow menus. However, what if you could speed up your TV in a matter of minutes? Among TV software DIYers, one of the latest trends involves using AI prompts to install alternate TV operating systems that eliminate ads and other tracking tools. Whether you’re an experienced vibes coder or simply sick of your Vizio’s ad banners, here’s what you need to know about installing your own TV operating system.

Stay tuned with CableTV.com

Get the latest deals, show premieres, and more by signing up for our newsletter.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

How does TV OS vibes coding work?

Via TechCrunch, developers like CleanYourTV and Vibes Launcher have released GitHub projects touting streamlined, ad-free interfaces. To install these projects on your TV, you’ll simply have to activate your TV’s developer access mode and have your AI assistant of choice automatically install the overlay on your home TV.

Vibe coded my parents’ TV this afternoon!

It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol https://t.co/E5Q4A1b0yI — Gathin (Ø,G) (@gathint) October 17, 2026

On the backend, most of these projects act as an alternative menu system layered on top of your TV’s stock setup. Depending on the exact overlay you install, you won’t need to root (i.e., permanently hack) your TV, and you can revert back to your TV’s original setup at any time.

Should you install a vibescoded TV OS on your TV?

Considering the amount of bloat on contemporary smart TVs, it’s easy to see the value of going with vibescoded alternatives. With annoyances ranging from pushy manufacturer ads to automatic content recognition for targeted ads, it’s no wonder folks prefer to go from stock overlays to something like this:

Finally got a little time to vibe-code my TV with Hermes and made something I actually want to look at.

No ads. No rows of movies to rent or things I don’t really care for. Just the apps I use, the time, the weather, and art from artists I love. https://t.co/Z57SHUNf7P — Jarlan Perez (@JarlanPerez) October 23, 2026

On the fence about trying an overlay for yourself? If you don’t know a code prompt from a hole in the ground, you might want to stick with app-based alternatives like ATV Launcher. These platforms are available directly on the Google Play Store and don’t require you to mess with AI and vibes coding. Similarly, be prepared to troubleshoot on your own and take on some risk. Compatibility varies widely by TV model and platform, and on social media, some users have reported Claude botching installations or needing more input to properly install a launcher.

What it means for you

The remote chance of government intervention notwithstanding, smart TV advertising won’t be going anywhere soon. Companies like Roku and Vizio are essentially advertising companies that sell TV hardware on the side, as ad revenue makes up a huge cut of their profits, and they’ll continue to highlight advertising on your TV screen. But the popularity of these vibescoded TV launcher projects reflects the discontent many consumers have with integrated and targeted advertising. We’re increasingly aware of how heavily technology tracks us, and few people like seeing targeted ads jump all the way from their browser to their TV screens. With the ubiquity of AI agents, we’ll be interested to see if alternative TV launchers become a more common way for shoppers to claw back some privacy from advertisers.

item.title: How To Watch the 2026 Midterm Elections
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Learn how to watch the midterm election results on Nov. 3 on CNN, Fox News, MS NOW, local channels, and free streams, with or without cable.
item.content:encoded:
Status: Verified 10/23/26

2026 midterm election channels

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and with all 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats, and 36 governors’ races on the ballot and Trump administration approval ratings at a nadir, it’ll be a hotly contested election. The good news is that U.S. election coverage airs on a wide variety of networks and free ad-supported TV (FAST) channels. Local ABC, CBS, NBC, Fox, and PBS coverage is free over the air where reception is available. You can also stream national election coverage for free through NBC News NOW, ABC News Live, CBS News 24/7, and LiveNOW from FOX. For CNN, Fox News, and MS NOW, you’ll need a live TV service or your favorite network’s new standalone app. The cable news channels and the Big Four national news channels will most likely have rolling midterm election coverage through the day and into the night, while your local affiliate channels will feature special coverage of the midterm election periodically throughout the evening. Scroll on to see how to watch the 2026 midterm election with or without cable and get the right TV setup thanks to our expert recommendations.

Find the best TV and internet providers near you

Enter your zip code below to see your neighborhood’s top-ranked TV and internet bundles

How to watch the 2026 midterm elections on cable news

How to watch cable news networks has evolved significantly over the past six years, so you’ll wanna weigh your options before signing up (yes, the paywalls still exist and are even more effective than ever) for a TV or streaming plan.

Cable TV and live TV streaming services

Pretty much every live TV provider carries CNN, Fox News, and MS NOW. The only major TV services that do not carry all three are Frndly TV, Fubo, and Philo. (Fubo carries Fox News, though.) We highly recommend YouTube TV for cord-cutters, Sling TV for bargain hunters, and Spectrum TV for cable diehards. For more recommendations, check out our annual Best of the Best Awards for TV Providers.

Standalone cable news apps

Sans a cable TV or live TV streaming plan, CNN All Access lets you stream live CNN coverage through CNN.com and the CNN app. HBO Max no longer carries CNN’s live news feed. Likewise, streaming FOX’s full midterm election coverage without a live TV plan requires FOX One, which offers a free trial. TV subscribers with Fox Business and Fox News in their lineup can also sign in to FOX One for free. In terms of MS NOW (formerly MSNBC), you can stream the midterm elections with a standalone MS NOW Membership. Just remember that Steve Kornacki is now part of NBC News’ election coverage team.

How to watch the 2026 midterms without cable

It’s 2026, so you have a ton of options to watch the midterm elections without a big, bad cable plan.

Over-the-air TV

A digital HD antenna usually costs under $50 and pulls in local affiliate channels for free. We highly recommend the Mohu Leaf 50 for its range, affordability, and compact design. Already have a digital antenna? Check your local ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, and PBS channel numbers to make sure you don’t miss any of the midterm results. You can verify available stations using Antennas Direct’s Transmitter Locator. Don’t have time to set up a digital antenna? You can stream some of your local affiliate channels, but it’ll cost you.

Local affiliate streaming options

  • ABC: N/A
  • CBS: Stream with Paramount+ Premium
  • FOX: Stream with FOX One
  • NBC: Stream with Peacock Premium Plus
  • PBS: Stream free at PBS.org

We recommend your local stream at PBS.org because it’s free and non-partisan. Oh, and remember that local affiliates are the only TV source for state, county, and ballot measure results.

Other free news streams

Beyond the free Big Four national streams mentioned in the intro, FAST services can help fill your midterm election gaps, too.

  • Tubi streams LiveNOW from FOX.
  • Pluto TV carries CNN Headlines, a curated news channel rather than CNN’s live cable feed.
  • The Roku Channel streams some local news channels.

And that’s just the tip of the iceberg. You can see more options in our guide to watching live TV news for free.

Featured in this article

YouTube TV

YouTube TV won our Best of the Best Award for live TV streaming services for the fifth year in a row. We love its channel lineup, multiview feature, and middle-of-the-road price point.

Sling TV

We don’t particularly love Sling TV, but it’s cheap as hell compared to other TV providers. Just be careful when picking a plan because they’re confusing and might not carry your favorite cable news channel.

How to watch the 2026 midterm elections FAQ

How can I watch the midterm election results for free?

Use an HD antenna for local network coverage, and then add free national news streams like NBC News NOW, ABC News Live, CBS News 24/7, and FOX LiveNow on Tubi.

Can I watch CNN election coverage without cable?

Yes. CNN All Access includes a 24/7 live feed of CNN, as do YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Sling TV, and DIRECTV (streaming plans).

Do I need FOX One to watch Fox News election coverage?

No. You can also watch Fox News through a TV package that carries the channel. Eligible subscribers can sign in to FOX One with their TV provider credentials at no extra cost.

Where can I watch local election results?

Local news stations typically cover state, county, and ballot measure races. You can watch through an antenna, participating station apps, or services like NewsON and Haystack News.

item.title: 9 Channels Will Air Super Bowl LXI, and Star Wars Is Involved
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Super Bowl LXI’s TV lineup expands to nine channels with a Star Wars alt-cast on Disney XD and a second Spanish-language broadcast on Univision.
item.content:encoded:
This week, ESPN announced that Super Bowl LXI will feature a Star Wars-themed alternate telecast on Disney Channel and Disney XD. The animated presentation will drop the live game straight into George Lucas’s Star Wars universe. That brings the total to nine U.S. TV channels showing the Big Game in some form. Fans can also stream the action through ESPN Unlimited, Disney+, and NFL+, though NFL+’s standard live-game streams are limited to phones and tablets. And no, these aren’t nine copies of the same broadcast. Between the traditional telecast, two Spanish-language productions, and several alternate presentations, ESPN is pulling out all the stops. Here’s what viewers can expect from each one.

Want more TV sports coverage?

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest event-viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Super Bowl LXI is heading to a galaxy far, far away

For some tuning in, Super Bowl LXI will take a detour through hyperspace on February 14, 2027. “Star Wars Funday Football” will recreate every play with animated NFL players, familiar galactic faces, and plenty of Easter eggs. The telecast will air on Disney Channel and Disney XD, with streaming available on Disney+ and the ESPN app. C-3PO is already confirmed, with original actor Anthony Daniels returning to voice the droid, while R2-D2 joins him in the teaser. The rest of the character lineup is still under wraps, but Darth Vader, Chewbacca, and Grogu would be welcome additions. Personally, I’m hoping for a Kit Fisto appearance.ESPN has already brought animated NFL games into the worlds of “Toy Story,” “The Simpsons,” and “Monsters, Inc.” But this will mark the company’s first animated alternate telecast of a Super Bowl. The timing couldn’t be better for Disney, either. A restored version of the original “Star Wars: A New Hope” returns to theaters just five days after the game as part of the franchise’s 50th-anniversary celebration. Ryan Gosling’s “Star Wars: Starfighter” follows on May 28, 2027. That’s quite the runway for building some galactic hype.

ESPN has even more Super Bowl alt-casts up its sleeve

ESPN airing its first Super Bowl was already a big deal. The network will share its traditional broadcast with ABC, featuring Joe Buck and Troy Aikman on the call. But Disney apparently decided one presentation wasn’t nearly enough. Its sprawling coverage is even frustrating some local ABC affiliates, who worry the additional viewing options will draw audiences and advertising revenue away from their stations, according to CNBC. ESPN2 will feature Peyton and Eli Manning’s signature “ManningCast” treatment. ESPNU gets “Super Bowl LXI Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show,” while NFL Network will air the analytics-heavy “Super Bowl LXI Playbook with Next Gen Stats.” ESPN Deportes will also carry its own Spanish-language broadcast. At this point, The Walt Disney Company is having itself a full-blown brand-apalooza. I’m half-expecting FX to unveil an “American Horror Story” alt-cast and Hulu to recruit the Kardashians for halftime analysis. Of course, I’m mostly kidding here. All told, Super Bowl LXI will air on ESPN, ABC, ESPN2, ESPNU, NFL Network, Disney Channel, Disney XD, and ESPN Deportes. That’s eight channels right there. And Univision brings the grand total to nine.

Univision is joining the Super Bowl party, too

Univision will air the Super Bowl for just the second time in its history. The Spanish-language network first carried the game in 2024 and is returning for Super Bowl LXI through a deal ESPN and TelevisaUnivision announced in May. And Univision won’t just carry ESPN Deportes’ feed. Both networks will produce their own Spanish-language broadcasts, complete with separate commentary teams. It’s a similar setup to Super Bowl LIX, when Fox Deportes and Telemundo offered distinct broadcasts en Español.

The Super Bowl’s streaming lineup gives you options

With nine TV channels airing Super Bowl LXI, cable, satellite, and live TV streaming providers will have plenty of coverage. Exactly which broadcasts you get depends on your package’s channel lineup, especially if you’re after a specific alt-cast. For viewers who’d rather stream directly, the three services below offer different ways to tune in.

ESPN Unlimited

ESPN Unlimited will stream Super Bowl LXI and ESPN’s alt-broadcasts through the ESPN app, from the “ManningCast” to “Star Wars Funday Football.”

Disney+

Disney+ will stream the Star Wars alt-cast alongside the traditional English-language telecast and ESPN Deportes’ Spanish-language broadcast. All U.S. subscribers can tune in without an ESPN Unlimited subscription.

NFL+

NFL+ lets subscribers watch Super Bowl LXI live on phones and tablets. It’s a convenient option for watching on the go, but its standard live-game streams aren’t available on connected TVs.

item.title: Fubo Adds Seven NBA Regional Sports Networks In These Markets
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Fubo has expanded the number of NBA regional sports networks it offers. Here are the seven new networks available and the NBA teams that are still missing.
item.content:encoded:
Former FanDuel Sports Network teams get new distribution agreements with Fubo

Nearly half of NBA teams found new local broadcast and streaming solutions after FanDuel Sports Network shut down. Some teams went the over-the-air (OTA) route, while others combined OTA with DAZN. Several popular TV plans either already carried the channels teams landed on, or made new or expanded deals with those franchises. Now there’s another live TV service in the mix. Fubo announced Thursday that it reached new distribution agreements with seven NBA teams and their regional sports networks (RSNs). Those teams include: the Atlanta Hawks, Charlotte Hornets, Detroit Pistons, Miami Heat, Milwaukee Bucks, Oklahoma City Thunder, and Orlando Magic. Fubo previously announced a deal to carry ClipperVision, the Los Angeles Clippers’ relaunched local broadcast network. The company said in a statement that the new agreements bring Fubo’s in-market coverage to more than 75% of U.S. NBA teams.

Want more TV sports coverage?

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest event-viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Which NBA teams don’t have agreements with Fubo?

Nearly 25% of the league isn’t represented on Fubo. That’s eight teams: the Cleveland Cavaliers, Indiana Pacers, Los Angeles Lakers, Memphis Grizzlies, Minnesota Timberwolves, San Antonio Spurs, Toronto Raptors, and Washington Wizards. The Raptors make sense — they’re in Canada, after all. Most of the remaining teams have exclusive deals with DAZN. Then there’s the Wizards. Fubo hasn’t offered Monumental Sports Network since 2024 due to a carriage dispute. The Lakers air on Spectrum SportsNet, which is one of the few RSNs Fubo has never carried.

item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: Recession indicator? The smash hit musical TV comedy “Glee” is getting a revival, with several original cast members returning. Read on for more info!
item.content:encoded:
The “Gleeboot” is real

The internet has been abuzz this year with rumors of a “Glee” revival. Those rumors were started by showrunner Ryan Murphy himself, who teased a reboot back in July and confirmed that he’d finished writing a new script in September. But even with a passionate showrunner, the show wasn’t officially greenlit yet. “Glee” was a 20th Television production, which means Disney owns it now (oh, think of all the licensed songs they could use!), and it was up to Disney to decide whether the revival would happen. Yesterday, Disney finally confirmed that the “Glee” reboot is indeed happening with a full series order, and when it airs, it’ll come to Disney+ and Hulu. Technically, Disney+ and Hulu are supposed to merge in the near future, so it’ll come to that combined streaming service, affectionately called “Hu Dis?” by Disney’s Canadian marketing team. In the meantime, the original “Glee” is streaming on both Disney+ and Hulu. So what will this new “Glee” show look like? Can anything top the original musical comedy show, which aired from 2009–2015 in an entirely different cultural climate? Keep reading, and I’ll go over everything we know so far and speculate on things to come.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Everything we know about the “Glee” revival

Several original cast members have agreed to reprise their roles, including Heather Morris (Brittany Pierce) and Chord Overstreet (Sam Evans). And of course, it wouldn’t be “Glee” without the queen of the Glee Club herself — Lea Michele is also set to return as Rachel Berry. That raises some questions about the structure of the show. This won’t be a true reboot, then — we’re not going to watch Kurt, Rachel, Quinn, and the rest go through high school again. Instead, it sounds like we’ll be following a new generation of glee club members in the present day, likely with some cameos from their school’s alumni. Maybe Rachel Berry will return from New York to teach at McKinley? Will she become the show’s new Mr. Schue? That’s just speculation, but the idea of Rachel Berry having to retire early from Broadway and become a high school teacher is kind of funny to me.

What songs will they sing in the new season?

There’s another, obvious question here that I think a lot of people are curious about: If this takes place in the present day, what songs will they sing? We don’t know anything for sure yet, but a lot has happened between the show’s March 2015 finale and now. Just as a reminder, here are some things that have gotten popular in that time frame:

  • “Hamilton” (September 2015)
  • “Shape of You” (January 2017)
  • “Old Town Road” (December 2018)
  • “bad guy” (March 2019)
  • “stupid horse” (May 2019)
  • “Say So” (January 2020)
  • “WAP” (August 2020)
  • “drivers license” (January 2021)
  • “Encanto” (November 2021)
  • “Espresso” (April 2024)
  • “Good Luck, Babe!” (April 2024)
  • “Not Like Us” (May 2024)
  • “Brat” (June 2024)
  • “KPop Demon Hunters” (June 2025)
  • “The Life of a Showgirl” (October 2025)
And that’s just in the music world. We’ve also had three presidential elections, a global pandemic, and the rise of AI. Teens use TikTok, shop for anti-aging cream at Sephora, and obsess over Nee-Doh squishies. Ryan Murphy could use any and all of these factors, mixing them together in his mind like a witch with a cauldron. We could get a production of “WAP” performed entirely in PPE and Covid masks, or Rachel Berry desperately trying to relate to kids with 6-7 jokes and a too-serious medley of “The Amazing Digital Circus” fan songs. We could get “Glee Hamilton.” The possibilities are as horrifying as they are endless. I just hope Darren Criss makes a return as well, if he gets a break from all of his successful Broadway shows. I know we were all watching for Blaine and The Warblers, anyway.

Where to catch up on “Glee”

Disney+

Disney+ is the place for all of Disney’s biggest IP — the streaming service you use every time there’s a new Star Wars or Marvel show. Anyone else been watching “VisionQuest?”

Hulu

Hulu is Disney’s other streaming service, and like Disney+, you can use it to watch “Glee.” Yes, this is redundant, but the two services are set to merge in the coming months anyways.

item.description: Don’t pay full price for live hoops. Learn how Prime Video and DIRECTV free trials give you the cheapest way to stream NBA games all season.
item.content:encoded:
You don’t need expensive cable to keep up with the NBA

As NBA media rights have fragmented across an expanding list of networks and streaming services, piecing together a setup to watch a full season of games gets expensive (and confusing) fast. Still, savvy fans can stack free trial offers and low-cost plans to build a solid lineup without breaking the bank. In our eyes, Amazon Prime Video offers one of the cheapest entry points for essential NBA streaming (and has a super-long free trial!), and when paired with other free trials like DIRECTV‘s, you can stream live hoops for a fraction of the cost. Keep reading for our picks for the best ways to stream the NBA on the cheap this season.

CableTV.com’s take: Stack free trials for the best savings

For budget-conscious bball fans, Amazon Prime Video is the streaming MVP this NBA season. Prime Video holds exclusive rights to Thursday and Friday night doubleheaders, the entire NBA Cup knockout stage, and the Play-In Tournament. If you don’t need a full Amazon Prime shopping membership (which is the best deal IMO), a standalone Prime Video plan costs just $8.99/mo.—or you can test-drive it with a 30-day free trial. Prime Video also acts as a hub where you can add a 7-day free trial of NBA League Pass to watch out-of-market games without juggling extra logins. To cover local regional sports networks (RSNs) and national channels like ABC, NBC, and ESPN, I say stack on a five-day free trial of DIRECTV. While DIRECTV’s CHOICE plan ($99.99/mo. after trial) is a high-tier investment—one we think is worth it for big sports fans—timing its trial during key rivalry weeks or Play-In games lets you watch complete live coverage across every core network at no cost.Need every NBA game out there? While combining Amazon Prime Video and DIRECTV covers a lot, you’ll need a few other services for total NBA coverage. item.title: Where NBA and NHL Teams Went After FanDuel Sports Network Closed
item.dc:creator: CableTV.com
item.description: FanDuel Sports Network is gone. Learn where affected NBA and NHL teams moved for local games, from DAZN and Prime Video to free over-the-air TV.
item.content:encoded:
NBA and NHL teams went to a mix of streaming services and free options

Financial problems led to the demise of both FanDuel Sports Network (FDSN) and Victory+ — two regional viewing options that allowed local fans to watch a bevy of NBA and NHL teams. With those platforms now gone, the affected teams had to quickly figure out where their games would air, and quickly. A total of 20 teams — 13 NBA, seven NHL — were affected by FDSN shutting down. In advance of the NBA and NHL regular seasons, CableTV.com reviewed every team that previously had media deals with FDSN and Victory+ and researched where they ended up. With so many channels and services out there, fans should know exactly where they can watch their favorite teams on TV. The NBA and NHL landed on a mix of streaming and over-the-air (OTA) solutions. Some made deals with DAZN, others went with Amazon Prime Video, and many went the free route.

Keep up with all the latest in entertainment news

Subscribe to CableTV.com's email newsletter for the latest TV event viewing guides, entertaining takes, and money-saving promotions.

By signing up, you agree to our Privacy Policy & Terms and Conditions.

Where former FanDuel Sports Network NBA teams went

NBA teams that moved to DAZN

Eight NBA teams signed deals with DAZN for their local broadcast streaming rights. That signals the strength DAZN has in the market as the London-based streaming company continues to explore widening its reach. Each team subscription starts at $19.99 per month, with higher-tier options available that include multiview features and additional streams. Several DAZN teams are also offering a limited number of games for free through local broadcast partners, even though DAZN remains their primary streaming home. The table below shows where fans can stream most local games for each affected team.

Team New streaming home Previous in-market home
Charlotte Hornets DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Southeast
Cleveland Cavaliers DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Ohio
Detroit Pistons DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Detroit
Indiana Pacers DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Indiana
Memphis Grizzlies DAZN FanDuel Sports Network South, FanDuel Sports Network Southeast
Minnesota Timberwolves DAZN FanDuel Sports Network North
Orlando Magic DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Florida
San Antonio Spurs DAZN FanDuel Sports Network Southwest

Data effective as of post date.

NBA teams that moved most local games to free over-the-air TV

Six teams made free over-the-air television their primary local broadcast home after FanDuel Sports Network closed. In one really fun case, a local station in Orlando rebranded to include the “Magic” name. This many NBA teams giving free access to games shows that it’s always been possible to create an inclusive, fan-centric viewing experience. But many franchises went the paid route, which has caused fans varying levels of frustration in recent years. In-market fans of the teams below can watch most games with a digital antenna or whichever TV provider they already have that carries those networks.

Team New OTA home Previous in-market home
Atlanta Hawks WANF (46) FanDuel Sports Network South, FanDuel Sports Network Southeast
Detroit Pistons WMYD TV20 (The Spot) FanDuel Sports Network Detroit
Charlotte Hornets WSOC-TV (ABC 9), WAXN-TV (64) FanDuel Sports Network Southeast
Miami Heat WPLG (10) FanDuel Sports Network Sun
Milwaukee Bucks WVTV-DT2 (My24) FanDuel Sports Network Wisconsin
Orlando Magic WRDQ-TV (27), WFTV (ABC 9) FanDuel Sports Network Florida
A note on the Hawks: On the day the regular season officially started, the team announced that its local streaming home will be Amazon Prime Video. Prime members in Atlanta’s broadcast market don’t need to pay for any additional subscription to access games.

Data effective as of post date.

The Oklahoma City Thunder did something a little different

The Thunder didn’t move to an OTA solution or DAZN. Instead, they essentially created their own regional sports network. The Thunder Gameday Network is anchored by the new Thunder+ standalone streaming service and two Griffin Media channels. Fans can stream any non-nationally televised game on Thunder+, while pay-TV customers can watch on KSBI (52) and KQCW (The CW 19) in Oklahoma City and Tulsa, respectively. An important note: KSBI and KQCW won’t carry every Thunder game free over the air. Ten regular-season games will be available OTA in Oklahoma City and Tulsa: six on KSBI and KQCW, plus four others on KWTV (9) and KOTV (6). That means local Thunder fans need Thunder+ or a participating TV provider to watch most in-market broadcasts.

What’s going on with the Los Angeles Clippers?

Good question. After weeks of wondering, we finally have an answer. The team unveiled the return of ClipperVision, a direct-to-consumer streaming service that folded into FanDuel Sports Network before last season. Fans can subscribe to that directly through the NBA app or watch it as a channel on DIRECTV, Fubo, and Spectrum. The team will also have 11 games air on KTLA. With the cap circumvention scandal and subsequent punishment, so many aspects of the franchise are still up in the air. But at least fans know where their team’s games will air in 2026–2027.

Where affected NHL teams went

NHL teams that chose Amazon Prime Video

Depending on the market, fans will need either a free Amazon account and a paid team-network subscription or an Amazon Prime membership that includes local games at no extra cost. We break down the differences in the table below. Keep in mind: Prime Video isn’t necessarily the only way to get these local broadcasts. Some team-branded networks are also available through participating TV providers like Fubo and Spectrum, while select games may air free over the air depending on the market.

Team New streaming home Previous in-market home Access
Anaheim Ducks Amazon Prime Video Victory+ Prime membership; no additional team subscription
Carolina Hurricanes Amazon Prime Video FanDuel Sports Network South Free Amazon account; paid team-network subscription
Columbus Blue Jackets Amazon Prime Video FanDuel Sports Network Ohio Free Amazon account; paid team-network subscription
Dallas Stars Amazon Prime Video Victory+ Prime membership; no additional team subscription
Minnesota Wild Amazon Prime Video FanDuel Sports Network North Free Amazon account; paid team-network subscription
St. Louis Blues Amazon Prime Video FanDuel Sports Network Midwest Free Amazon account; paid team-network subscription

Data effective as of post date.

Amazon already has rights to Thursday Night Football and several other sports, including the NBA and WNBA. The company’s move into regional broadcasting is an interesting development to watch, especially given what DAZN is currently trying to do in that space.

The Ducks also have a robust OTA offering

Anaheim is the only team of the six that will offer the majority of its 84-game schedule on OTA channels in tandem with Amazon. A total of 65 games will air on those channels: 61 on KCOP-TV (FOX Los Angeles+ 13) and four on KTTV (FOX 11). Fans can access OTA channels with a digital antenna or through a cable, satellite, or live TV streaming provider.

Kings, Predators, and Red Wings did it their own way

Three NHL teams found unique ways to address local broadcasting rights. The Los Angeles Kings went with DAZN for streaming, but still share the rebranded Angels Broadcast Television (ABTV) with the MLB’s Angels. The Nashville Predators expanded their partnership with Scripps Sports and went full OTA with WNPX-TV (The Spot – Nashville 28) and other channels. The Detroit Red Wings joined the MLB’s Tigers on a new RSN: Detroit SportsNet.

MLB teams also had to move broadcast providers

Earlier in the year, nearly one-third of Major League Baseball teams entered into new broadcast agreements after FanDuel Sports Network closed. Five teams partnered directly with MLB for local broadcast and distribution rights. Those teams were the Cincinnati Reds, Kansas City Royals, Miami Marlins, Milwaukee Brewers, and St. Louis Cardinals. The Tampa Bay Rays partnered with MLB, but also had their games distributed on other cable, satellite, and live TV streaming providers. The three other teams — Atlanta Braves, Detroit Tigers, and Los Angeles Angels — either created their own networks or joined newly formed ones.

What does this shift say about the future of sports broadcast rights?

FanDuel Sports Network’s collapse and the shakeup at Victory+ were significant developments in the sports-rights landscape. Regional sports networks have long been a fixture of local fandom, and these changes add even more complexity to a world that already has too many ways to watch sports and not enough clarity. RSN fees have been rising as more and more people cut the cord. FDSN’s collapse feels like another sign that the traditional RSN model is under serious pressure. In some ways, that’s good for fans. More free OTA access can mean fewer extra fees. But RSNs provided convenience and peace of mind, particularly for pay-TV customers whose plans already carried them. DAZN and Prime Video could be part of the solution. Then there’s newcomer BZZR. And of course, many teams have expanded partnerships with local over-the-air channels. All this to say that we’re living through a huge inflection point in local sports viewing where it seems like fans want fewer options, not more. That could be partly why the NBA is working toward a central streaming hub for in-market games. Whatever happens, it needs to happen relatively fast. Sports fans are getting fed up with all the changes and confusion. Just look at what’s happening with the Clippers.
